## System and Surroundings

![A simple energy balance diagram](figures/energy_balance_simple_diagram.svg){width=70% fig-align="center" #fig-simple_energy_balance_diagram}

An energy balance tracks energy entering / leaving the system and accumulation within the system.

## What is the system?

![The system and surroundings defines where the energy balance is applied](figures/system_surroundings.svg){width=70% fig-align="center" #fig-system_surroundings}

The system is the part that we are interested in studying. The surroundings are everything else.

## How systems store energy
A system can store energy in three ways:

::: {.incremental}
- Potential Energy, $E_p$
- Kinetic Energy, $E_k$
- Internal Energy, $U$
:::

## How systems gain or lose energy
A system can gain or lose energy in three ways:

::: {.fragment}
- Heat, $Q$
    - Energy transferred due to a temperature difference.
:::

::: {.fragment}
- Work, $W$
    - Energy transferred due to a force acting through a distance.
:::

::: {.fragment}
- Mass flow, $\dot{m}$
    - Energy carried by mass entering or leaving the system.
:::

## Energy Balance Diagram
![](figures/Energy_balance_diagram.svg){width=70% fig-align="center" #fig-Energy_balance_diagram}

$$\text{Energy In} - \text{Energy Out} = \text{Accumulation of Energy in the System}$$
$$\dot{E}_{in} + \dot{Q} + \dot{W} - \dot{E}_{out} = \frac{dE_{sys}}{dt}$$

## Heat and Work convention
!(figures/Energy_balance_diagram.svg){width=70% fig-align="center" #fig-Energy_balance_diagram}

::: {.callout-important}
## Important
Heat and work are defined as energy transfer *into* the system. If heat or work leaves the system, their values are negative.
:::

## Heat and work are quantities, not properties
Heat and work are not properties of a system. They are quantities that describe energy transfer across the system boundary.

::: {.callout-important}
## Important
Heat and work represent quantities of energy transfer. Heat is not stored in a system, and work is not stored in a system. When heat or work is transferred across the system boundary, the energy transferred is stored as $U$, $E_k$, or $E_p$.
:::
